name: evacuation_1812
_doc: The 15 August 1812 evacuation route and the zone the accounts place the attack in (T-0470). GENERATED by tools/derive_evacuation_1812.py from data/terrain/1812_evacuation_readings.json and three committed lines - do not hand-edit; --check re-derives it. Coordinates are EPSG:26916 metres; local ENU is these minus data/datum.json origin_utm_e / origin_utm_n. Documentary geography only: no figure, camp or event is staged by it.
review_note: Held for review because this record locates a battle fought by Potawatomi and allied warriors, and every account it reads was written by the garrison's side or by settler historians - none by the Potawatomi. That is the Indigenous-history review T-0472 gates the 1812 interpretive scene on. This file is geography only: it places a route and an evidence-weighted zone, stages nobody, depicts nobody, and quotes the printed accounts verbatim (their words, not this project's) only where a distance or a landform is read from them.
evidence_limit: No survey, map or marker of 1812 places the attack. The one distance is the commander's 'about a mile and a half', reached through a compilation's OCR; the one named place is a tradition recorded seventy years on. Measured along the reconstructed shore they disagree by 1456.2 m: Eighteenth Street lies 1053.8 m beyond the south end of the band that rounds to Heald's figure. That disagreement is drawn, not resolved.

disagreement.measure_note: Distances are measured along the traced waterline, as the mouth readings measure Swearingen's half mile. The trace wiggles: between the outlet and the seam row it is 11 per cent longer than its chord, so a distance walked on the beach lies between the along and straight figures. Eighteenth Street is beyond Heald's band on either measure.

properties.name: The evacuation route of 15 August 1812, fort to Eighteenth Street
properties.note: From the fort anchor down the old channel's west bank to the natural outlet, then south along the waterline: the derived 1812 shore to the seam row, a step of the stated length across the two traces' disagreement there, and the carried Rees 1849 shore below it. This is the line every distance below is measured along, and it is drawn on the reconstructed 1812 shore, not on modern streets. Two printed narratives agree on the shape - down the river to its mouth, then along the beach - and neither is a witness. Where the line lies on the ground is the derived 1812 shore north of Twelfth Street (inferred) and the carried Rees 1849 shore south of it, below which the 1812 terrain spec writes every vertex conjectural.

properties.name: North end of Heald's band (1.25 mi)
properties.note: A quarter of a mile either side. Heald writes 'about' and states the distance in half miles, so the reading is taken to mean the nearest half mile and the band is the interval that rounds to it, 1.25 to 1.75 miles. That is this project's reading of 'about', graded inferred; a tighter band would claim a precision the letter does not.

properties.name: Half a mile (Jordan, not adopted)
properties.note: Contemporary, and the editors print it among 'a few unmistakeable contemporary lies' (lines 8737-8738). Kept beside, not adopted: half a mile measured along the route ends at the river's natural outlet itself, before the beach every other account puts the attack on. Its station is drawn so the disagreement can be seen.

properties.name: The Eighteenth Street cottonwoods (tradition)
properties.note: Eighteenth Street's row, east of Prairie Avenue to the shore. Arnold names the street ('leading from Michigan avenue to the lake') and puts the tree 'not very far from the track of the Illinois Central', which ran along the lake end; Prairie's committed crossing is taken as the locus's west limit for that reason. No easting is stated for either tree, so the locus is a line along the street and not a point. Drawn along the row's northing; the street's small departure from due east is not modelled. A tradition, recorded in the 1880s and 1890s, carried by the Kinzie family and by one unnamed Potawatomi witness relayed second-hand. Juliette Kinzie's 'saplings at the time' is a statement about the trees, not about the battle. It is the one reading that names a place, and it lies further south than the distance reading allows - see the derived file's disagreement - so it is kept beside the distance and neither is preferred.

properties.name: Where the accounts place the attack of 15 August 1812
properties.note: The strip between the waterline and the ridge line, from the north end of Heald's band to Eighteenth Street's south line. Its north part is the distance reading (2012-2816 m along the route); its south end is the tradition (3870 m along). They disagree by 1456.2 m, so the zone spans both and prefers neither, and NO POINT INSIDE IT IS CLAIMED. The fight round the wagons in the rear, the charge up the bank and the parley all fall within it on the accounts read; Heald's withdrawal 'out of shot of the bank' lay inland of it at no stated distance and is not drawn. The zone is the strip from the waterline back to the ridge line - 100 yards, Quaife's figure and the wider of the two - because both readings put the attackers 'behind the bank' and the column on the beach in front of it, so the attack stood between the water and the ridge. The 1895 editors' 'a hundred feet or more' is the bank's near face and falls inside the strip. Offset due west, the land side, rather than square to the shore; where the shore runs about 13 degrees east of south that makes the strip about 2.5 per cent narrower measured square to it.
